Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:11:1.english: Wealthy - A wealthy person whom [people] assess [as having] silver vessels.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:1:1.hebrew: ד"ה משלם מה שבתוכו - רבא מתרץ לה לטעמיה, בכלים שדרכן להטמין בגדיש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:1:1.english: [Regarding the words] He pays what is inside it - Rava explains it according to his own reasoning, [as referring] to utensils that are normally hidden in a stack [of grain].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:2:1.hebrew: אלא דמי גדיש - אם הבעירו בעל השדה, דלא קביל עליה אלא נטירותא דגדיש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:2:1.english: Only the value of a stack - If the owner of the field burned it, for he only accepted upon himself the guarding of a stack.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:2:2.hebrew: חטין וחיפן בשעורים - אע"פ שנותן לו רשות לחטין, אינו משלם אלא שעורין, דאמר ליה: לא ראיתי אלא שעורין, לפיכך לא נזהרתי בהן כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:2:2.english: Wheat and covered them with barley - Even though he gave him permission for wheat, he pays only [for] barley, for he says to him: "I saw only barley; therefore I was not so careful with it."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:3:1.hebrew: מאי הוה ליך גביה דאזקתיה - בידים, ששרפתו או שהשלכתו לים. ולא דמי למשאיל מקום לחבירו להגדיש שעורין והגדיש חטים, דאמרן לעיל אינו משלם אלא דמי שעורין, דמבעיר לא מזיק בידים הוא אלא פושע, כדכתיב "כי תצא אש" — מעצמה. מפי המורה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:3:1.english: What [business] did you have with it that you damaged it - [Meaning] directly with [your] hands, that you burned it or threw it into the sea. And this is not comparable to one who lends a space to his fellow to stack barley and he stacked wheat, where we said above [that] he pays only the value of barley; because one who kindles a fire is not one who damages directly with [his] hands, but rather negligent, as it is written: "If fire break out" — [that is,] on its own. [This is] from the mouth of [my] teacher.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:3:2.english: [If] she was negligent with it - She did not guard it in the manner of guardians, and it was lost.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:4:1.english: [With that of Rava] you teach it - You say it in the name of Rava.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:4:2.english: Barley and covered them with wheat - [He] gives him permission to stack barley, and not wheat.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:5:1.hebrew: שמעית מילתא לר' יהודה - אליבא דר' יהודה דמתני':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:5:1.english: I heard a matter regarding Rabbi Yehuda - According to Rabbi Yehuda of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:5:2.hebrew: עשו תקנת נגזל באשו - כי היכי דתקנו רבנן לנגזל לישבע כמה גזלו ויטול, דתנן במסכת שבועות (דף מד:): "אלו נשבעין ונוטלין: השכיר והנגזל", כך תקנו באשו שישבע מה הטמין ויטול:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:5:2.english: They applied the ordinance of a robbery victim to his fire - Just as the Sages instituted for a robbery victim to take an oath [as to] how much was robbed from him and collect [it] — as we learned in a Mishnah in tractate Shevuot (44b): "These take an oath and collect: the hired laborer and the robbery victim" — so too they instituted regarding his fire, that he takes an oath [as to] what he concealed and collects [it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:6:1.hebrew: אליבא דמ"ד לא דיינינן דינא דגרמי - בפרק הגוזל ומאכיל (לקמן בבא קמא דף קיז:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:6:1.english: According to the one who says we do not judge liability for indirect damage - In the chapter [entitled] HaGozel UMa'akhil (below, Bava Kamma 117b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62a:8:1.english: In a chest - A box in which money is placed.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:10:1.hebrew: מי מנחי אינשי מרגניתא בכספתא או לא - אפילו יש עדים שהיה בו מרגניתא מבעיא ליה, דשמא לא אבעי ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה להאי, ולא אמרינן מאי הוה ליה גביה דאזקיה, כיון דלא רגילי אינשי לאנוחי כלל. ולא דמי לדינר זהב דלעיל, דאבעי לה לאסוקי אדעתא טפי, דפעמים שאומר כן, דירא שאם היתה יודעת שהוא של זהב לא היתה שומרתו; ולא דמי נמי לארנקי בגדיש, דרגילין טפי דמנחי מרגניתא בכספתא. ואין לפרש דלענין שבועה מבעיא ליה, אי עשו תקנת נגזל ויהא נאמן לומר שהיה בו מרגניתא, דא"כ, מה היה אומר לרב אשי: "לאו היינו מתני'"? מה ענין זה למשנתינו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:10:1.english: Do people place pearls in a safe or not? - Even if there are witnesses that there was a pearl in it, he raises the dilemma, for perhaps this [damager] did not need to anticipate this, and we do not say, "What business did he have with him that he damaged it?" since people are not accustomed to place [pearls in a safe] at all. And it is not comparable to the golden dinar [mentioned] above, for she should have anticipated [that] more, since sometimes [the depositor] says so because he fears that if she knew it was of gold, she would not guard it; and it is also not comparable to a purse in a stack of grain, for people are more accustomed [to that than] to placing pearls in a safe. And one should not explain that he raises the dilemma regarding an oath — whether they enacted the ordinance of a robbery victim [here] so that he would be believed to say that there was a pearl in it — for if so, what would he be saying to Rav Ashi: "Is this not the Mishnah?" What connection does this have to our Mishnah?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:12:1.hebrew: מה בין גזלן לחמסן - בלישנא דקרא אין חילוק ביניהם, והכא קבעי: מה בין גזלן דרבנן לחמסן דרבנן? דתניא בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה:): "הוסיפו עליהם הגזלנים והחמסנים". ומפרש: גזלן לא יהיב דמי, ובמציאת חרש שוטה וקטן, כדמוקי ליה התם, דאין פסול מן התורה אלא משום דרכי שלום:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:12:1.english: What is [the difference] between a gazlan and a chamsan? - In the language of Scripture there is no distinction between them, and here [the Gemara] asks: what is [the difference] between a rabbinic gazlan and a rabbinic chamsan? For it was taught in a baraita in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25b): "They added to them the gazlanim and the chamsanim." And [the Gemara here] explains: a gazlan does not give money — and [this refers to] a lost object [found by] a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, as [the Gemara] establishes it there, for he is not disqualified by Torah law, [since taking it is prohibited] only on account of [preserving] ways of peace.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:12:2.hebrew: חמסן יהיב דמי - וכשלא אמר "רוצה אני", כדמפרש. אבל מן התורה אינו פסול אלא היכא דלא יהיב דמי, אבל היכא דיהיב דמי כשר, אע"ג דלא אמר "רוצה אני". אע"פ שעובר על לאו ד"לא תחמוד", הא אמרי' בפרק שנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף ה: ושם ד"ה בלא): "לא תחמוד" לאינשי בלא דמי משמע להו. וההיא דסוף מכילתין (דף קיט.) דמייתי מחמס בני יהודה, דאפילו היכא דיהיב דמי הוה כאלו נוטל נשמתו — לאו דרשה גמורה היא, אלא אסמכתא בעלמא, דחמסן דקרא היינו גזלן דלא יהיב דמי. וא"ת: כיון דחמסן דיהיב דמי פסול מדרבנן, א"כ כי אמרי' בפ' שנים אוחזין (ב"מ ד' ה: ושם ד"ה בלא): "אלא הא דאמר רב הונא: משביעים אותו שבועה שאינה ברשותו — נימא מיגו דחשיד כו'", ומשני: "מורה ואומר דמי קיהיבנא" — מ"מ מה תירץ בכך? אם הוא מעכב הפקדון בידו ורוצה ליפטר בדמים בעל כרחו של בעלים, הרי הוא חמסן ופסול לשבועה מדרבנן, ואכתי נימא "מיגו דחשיד כו'"! וי"ל: דמ"מ בגזלן דאורייתא אין להוכיח שלא יהא חשוד אשבועתו. ועוד, דחמסן דרבנן כשר הוא, ואינו פסול עד שיכריזו עליו, כדאמר בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין ד' כו:). ואפילו אם הוא ידוע שנעשה חמסן בענין זה, שמא לא ראו חכמים לפוסלו בכך וגם לא להכריז, אלא דוקא כי שקיל וחטיף בזרוע בעל כרחייהו דבעלים. והמקשה דקא פריך "נימא מיגו דחשיד כו'", אע"ג דהא ודאי קים לן דגזלן דרבנן בעי הכרזה ואינו נפסל עד אחר הכרזה, כל עיקר לא הביא דברי רב הונא אלא משום דמקשה "והא קעבר בלא תחמוד". א"נ, הכי מקשה: כיון שפטר עצמו במה שטען "נגנבו" או "נאבדו", ואינו משלם דמים אלא לפי שאינו רוצה לישבע, ואם היה פוטרו מן השבועה לא היה משלם כלום — א"כ נימא "מיגו כו'". ומשני: "מורה ואומר כו'", וגם אם היה פוטרו מן השבועה, שמא כמו כן היה משלם דמים לפי שמעכב הפקדון בידו, ולהכי לא חשיד אממונא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:12:2.english: A chamsan gives money - And [this is] when [the owner] did not say, "I want [to sell]," as [the Gemara] explains. However, by Torah law one is disqualified only where he does not give money, whereas where he gives money he is qualified, even though [the owner] did not say, "I want [to sell]." Even though he violates the prohibition of "You shall not covet," behold we say in the chapter [entitled] Shenayim Ochazin (Bava Metzia 5b, and there s.v. Belo): "You shall not covet" implies to people [taking] without money. And that [teaching] at the end of our tractate (119a) which cites from "the violence of the children of Judah," that even where one gives money it is as though he takes his soul — that is not a full-fledged exposition, but a mere scriptural support (asmakhta), for the chamsan of the verse is a gazlan who does not give money. And if you ask: Since a chamsan who gives money is disqualified by rabbinic law, if so, when we say in the chapter [entitled] Shenayim Ochazin (Bava Metzia 5b, and there s.v. Belo): "Rather, [what about] that which Rav Huna said: We administer an oath to him that [the deposit] is not in his possession — let us say, since (migo) he is suspected [of monetary dishonesty] etc.," and [the Gemara] answers: "He rationalizes and says, 'I am giving money'" — nevertheless, what did [the Gemara] answer by this? If he withholds the deposit in his possession and wishes to discharge himself with money against the owner's will, he is a chamsan and is disqualified from taking an oath by rabbinic law, and still let us say, "Since he is suspected etc."! And one can answer: That in any case, regarding a gazlan by Torah law, one cannot prove [from Rav Huna's ruling] that he is not suspected regarding his oath. And furthermore, a chamsan by rabbinic law is qualified, and he is not disqualified until they proclaim [his disqualification] publicly, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26b). And even if it is known that he became a chamsan in this manner, perhaps the Sages did not see fit to disqualify him for this nor to proclaim [against him], except specifically when he takes and snatches by force against the owners' will. And the questioner who objects, "Let us say, since he is suspected etc.," even though we certainly know that a gazlan by rabbinic law requires a public proclamation and is not disqualified until after the proclamation — the entire reason he brought Rav Huna's statement was only because he objects, "But he violates 'You shall not covet'!" Alternatively, he asks as follows: Since he exempted himself by claiming "they were stolen" or "they were lost," and he only pays money because he does not want to swear, and if one were to exempt him from the oath he would not pay anything — if so, let us say, "Since [he is suspected] etc." And [the Gemara] answers: "He rationalizes and says etc.," and even if one were to exempt him from the oath, perhaps he would likewise pay money since he is withholding the deposit in his possession, and therefore he is not suspected of [stealing] money.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:1:1.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים במדליק בתוך שלו והלכה ודלקה בתוך של חברו אבל במדליק בתוך של חבירו משלם כל מה שבתוכו - כלומר, בדבר שדרכו, כגון מוריגים וכלי בקר; אבל ארנקי בגדיש — לא מחייבי רבנן. אע"פ שדקדקנו בכל הני דלעיל שיהא משלם כל מה שבתוכו לרבנן כמו לר' יהודה, הני מילי היכא דקתני "ומודים" או היכא דקתני "דברי הכל", אבל הכא "במה דברים אמורים" קתני, ורבנן מילתייהו מפרשי ולאו אמילתא דרבי יהודה קיימי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:1:1.english: "In what case are these things said? When one kindles [a fire] within his own [property], and it went and burned within his fellow's [property]; but when one kindles [a fire] within his fellow's [property], he pays for everything that is inside it" - That is to say, [he is liable] for something that is customary [to be kept in a stack], such as threshing sledges and cattle implements; however, [for] a purse in a stack, the Rabbis do not hold [him] liable. Even though we inferred in all those [cases] above that he pays for everything inside it according to the Rabbis just as according to Rabbi Yehuda, that applies where [the text] teaches "and they agree" or where it teaches "all agree"; however, here it teaches "In what case are these things said?", and the Rabbis are explaining their own statement, and are not addressing Rabbi Yehuda's statement.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:2:1.hebrew: שאינו משלם אלא דמי שעורים - במדליק בתוך שלו איירי, דאי במדליק בתוך של חבירו, שעורין והגדיש חטין למה לא ישלם חטין, כיון דחזי להו? ובסמוך מדמי להו נמי לנותן דינר זהב לאשה ופשעה בו; משמע דהיינו מדליק בתוך שלו והלכה בתוך של חברו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:2:1.english: That he pays only the value of barley - [The Gemara] is speaking of one who lights [a fire] within his own [property], for if [it were speaking] of one who lights [a fire] within his fellow's [property], [in the case where he was permitted to stack] barley and he stacked wheat, why would he not pay [for] wheat, since he sees it? And shortly [below, the Gemara] also compares them to one who gives a gold dinar to a woman and she was negligent with it; [this] implies that this [case] is one who lights [a fire] within his own [property] and [the fire] went into his fellow's [property].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:5:1.hebrew: לרבי יהודה דמחייב על נזקי טמון באש כו' - לרבנן נמי הוה מצי למימר דעשו תקנה בבירה בכל דבר, ובגדיש במוריגין; אלא רבותא אשמועי', דלרבי יהודה אפי' ארנקי בגדיש עשו תקנת נגזל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:5:1.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, who deems [one] liable for concealed [articles] damaged by a fire, etc. - According to the Rabbis as well, [Shmuel] could have said that they instituted the ordinance for [articles in] a mansion regarding any item, and for [articles in] a grain stack regarding threshing sledges; rather, he teaches us a novel point: that according to Rabbi Yehuda, even [for] a purse in a grain stack they applied the ordinance of a robbery victim.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:6:1.hebrew: עשו תקנת נגזל במסור או לא - כתב רב אלפס: כגון שיש עדים שמסרו ואיבד ממונו, ואין יודעין כמה; תיקו, וכל תיקו דממונא לקולא. ובשם רב האי גאון כתוב: שישבע ויטול מחצה, שכל תיקו דממונא חולקין; ואין נראה לר"י לחייב כלל משום תיקו. ור"ת מפרש דהך בעיא כשהמוסר מכחיש את הנמסר, דומיא דנגזל בשבועות דגזלן מכחישו, אבל אם המוסר עצמו אינו יודע כמה — ישבע נמסר כמה הפסיד ויטול. ולר"י נראה דהך בעיא אפילו אין המוסר יודע, דומיא דתקנת נגזל באשו שאין המבעיר יודע כמה הפסיד הניזק, דמבעי ליה במסור אי עשו תקנתא או לא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62a:6:1.english: "Did they apply the ordinance of a robbery victim in [the case of] an informer, or not?" - Rav Alfasi wrote: [This refers to a case] where there are witnesses that he informed on him and caused the loss of his property, but they do not know how much [was lost]; [the Gemara concludes] teiku [let it stand unresolved], and every teiku regarding monetary matters is [ruled] leniently [exempting the defendant]. And in the name of Rav Hai Gaon it is written that he swears and collects half, for [in] every teiku regarding monetary matters, they divide [the disputed sum]; however, it does not appear [correct] to Ri to obligate [payment] at all on account of a teiku. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that this query [applies] when the informer contradicts the one informed upon, similar to [the case of] a robbery victim in [tractate] Shevuot, where the robber contradicts him; however, if the informer himself does not know how much [was lost], the one informed upon swears how much he lost and collects. But to Ri it appears that this query [applies] even when the informer does not know, similar to the ordinance of a robbery victim regarding one's fire, where the one who kindled [the fire] does not know how much the injured party lost, for [the Gemara] asks regarding an informer whether they enacted the ordinance or not.
